document.title: Excerpt from Statement of the Soviet Military Command in Afghanistan on the Withdrawal of Soviet Troops, February 14, 1989
document.authors: Soviet Military Command in Afghanistan / USSR Defense Ministry
document.publisher: National Security Archive (GWU), Afghanistan and the Soviet Withdrawal 1989 20 Years Later
document.note: Statement delivered to the head of the UN Mission in Afghanistan on Feb 14, 1989. It reviews Soviet-Afghan relations before 1979, justifies sending troops after repeated Afghan requests, criticizes US arming of the opposition despite the Geneva agreements, and rejects Vietnam comparisons.

sources_cited: Alexander Lyakhovsky, Tragedy and Valor of Afghan, Iskon, Moscow 1995, Appendix 11
key_claims: The Soviet command says the withdrawal was planned and in accordance with the Geneva Agreements, not a flight like the American withdrawal from Vietnam.
The Soviets reject Vietnam analogies as unfair and absurd, saying they were invited by the Afghan government.
The statement accuses the U.S. of arming the opposition in violation of the Geneva agreements, destabilizing Afghanistan.
The Soviets claim to have transferred property worth over 830 million rubles to the Afghan people during withdrawal.
The Soviet command says it sought to prevent the withdrawal from sparking civil war and pledged continued help for a political settlement.
